mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% in a single month (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent decline in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decline for three consecutive months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over six months signals robust demand growth, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and HOUST co-move upward for six months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings growth offsets cost pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during sustained above-average payroll employment growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months, coupled with a flat or declining consumption series (GDPC1), signals a savings glut that depresses demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently above its moving average and GDPC1 is flat or declining (p > 0.10).
